forces.title: Hyperscale cloud providers and AI demand driving rapid capacity expansion.
forces.description: The current growth cycle for data centres is increasingly driven by hyperscale cloud providers, global content platforms, and AI-first companies. This shift represents a structural change from historical colocation facilities and demands higher rack densities, resilient power architectures, and advanced cooling solutions, accelerating the need for large-scale infrastructure investments across India.
forces.source_title: India data centre opportunity - From emerging demand hub to integrated data centre powerhouse

forces.title: India's low construction costs, affordable power, and talent attract DC investment.
forces.description: India offers distinct competitive advantages, including being the second most cost-effective location for data centre construction globally (Mumbai), highly affordable electricity tariffs (USD7.5-8/kWh), and a large, cost-efficient IT and AI talent pool. Additionally, the country boasts abundant renewable energy sources (50% of installed capacity by mid-2025) and earmarked land parcels with state incentives, significantly lowering development costs and accelerating project execution.
forces.source_title: India data centre opportunity - From emerging demand hub to integrated data centre powerhouse

forces.title: Robust connectivity and local supply chain strengthen data centre development.
forces.description: India's data centre growth is bolstered by a developing infrastructure network, including 17+ international subsea cables and expanding fibre networks, ensuring strong domestic and international connectivity. A well-established base of local contractors and equipment suppliers across power, cooling, and construction segments, coupled with global players investing in local manufacturing and SEZ incentives, reduces lead times and costs, enhancing execution efficiency for scalable data centre projects.
forces.source_title: India data centre opportunity - From emerging demand hub to integrated data centre powerhouse

forces.title: Government policies and tax breaks attract significant investment into data centres.
forces.description: The Indian government provides strong policy support, including 100% FDI under the automatic route for data centres. Fiscal incentives like waivers on electricity and stamp duties, aggressive tax holidays under Section 80-IA, and Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes for domestic component manufacturing significantly improve the financial upside for operators. Additionally, long-term tax clarity for foreign cloud service providers and a 15% safe harbour margin for Indian data centre entities enhance tax certainty and competitiveness.

forces.title: AI-driven workloads necessitate fundamental redesign of data centre infrastructure.
forces.description: Artificial intelligence is fundamentally altering data centre design, moving from CPU-led, air-cooled setups with low-power racks (8-12 kW) to GPU-driven, liquid-cooled architectures with high-density racks (50-60 kW) and ultra-low-latency fiber. This shift requires significant upgrades in structural capacity, power, cooling, and energy sourcing, representing a full-scale redesign rather than incremental upgrades, thereby redefining capital intensity and operational requirements for DC operators.
forces.source_title: India data centre opportunity - From emerging demand hub to integrated data centre powerhouse

forces.title: Sustainability and renewable energy adoption are becoming core for data centres.
forces.description: Data centre operators are increasingly prioritizing sustainability through renewable energy adoption, efficiency improvements, and advanced cooling technologies. This global trend, driven by rising power intensity and stakeholder focus on environmental impact, is aimed at reducing carbon footprints, meeting regulatory expectations, and aligning with net-zero emissions commitments. While global majors lead, Indian operators are establishing clear pathways to greener operations, requiring sustained capital expenditure and ecosystem collaboration.
forces.source_title: India data centre opportunity - From emerging demand hub to integrated data centre powerhouse

forces.title: Over USD120 billion committed by major players driving market expansion.
forces.description: Global hyperscalers, international data centre operators, and Indian conglomerates have collectively committed over USD120 billion in investments to the India market. This significant capital allocation indicates strong conviction in India’s role in the regional and global digital infrastructure landscape. The investments are increasingly directed towards AI-ready data centres, optimized for GPU-intensive workloads, signaling a transition from incremental expansion to large-scale, strategic growth.
forces.source_title: India data centre opportunity - From emerging demand hub to integrated data centre powerhouse

forces.title: Data protection act mandates local data residency, boosting domestic DC demand.
forces.description: The Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act 2023 significantly impacts data centre real estate by limiting cross-border data transfers. This regulation compels global enterprises to establish a physical data residency footprint within India, thereby acting as a powerful driver for increased domestic data centre demand and construction. This also creates opportunities for specialized advisory services to design compliant architectures.
forces.source_title: India’s data centre revolution: The integrated lifecycle blueprint (2026-2030)

forces.title: Wartime conditions introduce new kinetic, cyber-physical risks to data centre operations.
forces.description: Geopolitical conflicts introduce an expanded threat landscape for data centres, including kinetic risks, cyber-physical attacks, infrastructure interdependencies, and prolonged supply chain disruptions. These conditions can simultaneously impact power availability, network connectivity, cooling systems, employee access, and recovery capabilities, necessitating a shift from uptime-optimized architectures to designs engineered for endurance, survivability, and sustained operation under stress, significantly increasing design complexity and cost.
forces.source_title: Data centres on the frontline: Building resilience in a war environment

forces.title: Fragmented service ecosystem hinders efficient data centre scaling and delivery.
forces.description: The exponential growth in India's digital infrastructure is met with significant complexity due to fragmented service providers operating in silos across construction, technology, and cooling. This "Integration Gap" leads to delays, muddied responsibilities, and inefficiencies in meeting demand. Overcoming this requires a shift towards integrated 'Lifecycle Partners' that can manage every phase of data centre development and operation, posing a substantial delivery risk if not addressed.
forces.source_title: India’s data centre revolution: The integrated lifecycle blueprint (2026-2030)

forces.title: Existing infrastructure unprepared for power-intensive AI workloads.
forces.description: Many older Indian data centre facilities rely on legacy air-cooling designs that are insufficient for the intense heat generated by modern GPU clusters and AI workloads. This "AI Readiness Gap" necessitates a significant engineering and multi-stakeholder delivery risk involving a shift from standard raised floors to advanced liquid cooling and new high-density power sourcing. This transformation is critical for operational viability and commercial competitiveness of future data centres.
forces.source_title: India’s data centre revolution: The integrated lifecycle blueprint (2026-2030)

forces.title: Advancements in DC architecture create opportunities for domestic manufacturing.
forces.description: The rapid advancements in data centre architecture, particularly with the emergence of AI-native designs, present a strategic opportunity for domestic players to localize manufacturing across the value chain. While some segments are dominated by global incumbents, whitespaces are emerging for Indian companies to invest in expanding capabilities organically or through strategic partnerships for racks, cooling, and power systems, making a competitive domestic supply chain integral to India's data centre ambitions.
forces.source_title: India data centre opportunity - From emerging demand hub to integrated data centre powerhouse

viewpoints.title: India's data centre market poised for exponential growth and global hub status.
viewpoints.description: India's data centre market is projected to double its global share from 2-3% in FY26 to ~5% by FY30, with market size growing from USD1.7 billion to USD6.8 billion. This growth is driven by significant domestic capacity expansion (4.5 GW pipeline over five years) and structural advantages like low construction costs, affordable renewable power, and a deep talent pool, positioning India as a prominent APAC data centre hub.
viewpoints.source_title: India data centre opportunity - From emerging demand hub to integrated data centre powerhouse

viewpoints.title: AI and HPC workloads to drive 10x data centre capacity growth over next decade.
viewpoints.description: India's data centre capacity is expected to increase tenfold over the next decade, fueled by an exponential surge in AI and High-Performance Computing (HPC) workloads. These workloads are 5-10 times more power-intensive than traditional cloud uses, forcing a fundamental redesign of data centre architecture towards higher rack densities, advanced cooling, and increased capital intensity per MW. This marks a shift to large-scale capacity creation.
viewpoints.source_title: India data centre opportunity - From emerging demand hub to integrated data centre powerhouse

viewpoints.title: India offers unique cost, land, and power advantages for data centre development.
viewpoints.description: India possesses significant supply-side advantages distinguishing it from competing global data centre destinations. These include Mumbai being the world’s second most cost-effective location for data centre construction, exceptionally affordable electricity tariffs (USD7.5-8/kWh), abundant renewable energy sources (50% of 500 GW installed capacity), and a large, cost-efficient IT and AI talent pool. These factors underpin India's strong competitiveness in the global market.
viewpoints.source_title: India data centre opportunity - From emerging demand hub to integrated data centre powerhouse

viewpoints.title: India's data centre market requires integrated lifecycle partners to overcome complexity.
viewpoints.description: India's digital infrastructure is undergoing rapid expansion, driven by data localization, AI workloads, and 5G. However, the biggest challenge to scaling is the complexity of demand, exacerbated by fragmented service providers. The market needs true 'Lifecycle Partners' offering seamless services from planning and building to deployment, operations, and maintenance, covering high-value areas like Capital Markets, Telecom, Digital Transformation, and ESG frameworks.
viewpoints.source_title: India’s data centre revolution: The integrated lifecycle blueprint (2026-2030)

viewpoints.title: India's REIT market poised for rapid expansion, reaching USD123 billion by 2029.
viewpoints.description: India’s Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) sector surpassed a USD11.43 billion market capitalization in November 2025 and is projected to expand significantly to USD123 billion by 2029. This growth is anticipated to be driven by institutional demand, particularly in office and retail assets, with expectations of 25-30% penetration in the office segment by 2030 and at least one new REIT launching annually for the next 3-5 years.

Significant spend on grid and upstream infrastructure (substations, transmission lines) and internal DC equipment (UPS, batteries, gensets, switchgears).
Growing demand for ongoing maintenance and support of complex data centre infrastructure.

This opportunity spans design & construction, power infrastructure (outside and inside DC), cooling systems, and network infrastructure.
